FEDERAL POWER COMMISSION BUREAU OF POWER
Final Environmental Impact Statement
SUMMARY SHEET
1. This is an Administrative Action.
Description of the action: Duke Power Company (Applicant) has filed for Commission approval an application for a major license for construction, operation, and maintenance of the proposed Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project No. 2740 to be located on Bad Creek and West Bad Creek in Oconee County, South Carolina and to determine what conditions, if any, should be included in any license issued for this project. The project would consist of a 318-acre upper reservoir (full pond elevation of 2,310 feet) located within the drainage of Bad and West Bad Creeks, a 1-1/4-mile-long underground power tunnel, a 1,000-MW underground powerhouse complex with 4 reversible pump turbine units rated at 250 MW each, and discharge into the existing 7,565-acre lower reservoir, Lake Jocassee (full pond elevation of 1,110 feet). The upper reservoir would inundate about 370 acres, with an additional 315 acres disrupted by transmission line construction, 40 acres cleared for temporary use during construction, and 95 acres used for tunnel portals, access roads, and switchyard area. A 525-kV transmission line would run from the Bad Creek Project area to the Oconee Nuclear Station switchyard via new and existing rights-of-way. In addition, a 100-kV transmission line would be constructed in new and existing rights-of-way from the Bad Creek switchyard to the existing Jocassee Pumped Storage Project switchyard. The 525-kV line would be used to convey Bad Creek project pumping and generated power, while the 100-kV line would serve to provide power during construction and later as an emergency power source to the Bad Creek Project. No recreational facilities are proposed within the project area. The upper reservoir would be fenced to preclude public access due to water level fluctuations of up to 160 feet per week. Applicant would compensate for the loss of existing recreation by construction of a 30-mile hiking trail with shelters.
